expected: Either specs/backlog/ gets an explicit opt-in (backlog is PM-curated repository truth per backlog-ownership + release-governance, and the BL-* chokepoint/CI checks become real), or backlog is formally declared workspace-private and the pre-commit scope, CI job, and force-added stray are removed — one consistent story.
notes: Found 2026-07-02 while sanitizing the backlog: deletions/creations of backlog entries leave no git trace, which is how consumed/stale slop accumulated invisibly. Disposition decision is the operator's (privacy vs governance).
repro: git check-ignore -v specs/backlog/candidates.md -> .gitignore /specs/* ; git ls-files specs/backlog/ -> a single force-added file; compare with the negation block that opts in bugs/audits/memory.

symptom: The broad /specs/* privacy ignore opts back in constitution, memory, audits *.md, bugs *.md/*.jsonl, releases/ACTIVE.md — but NOT specs/backlog/. Every live backlog entry is untracked+ignored; exactly one stray file was historically force-added. The pre-commit backlog-doctor scope (commits touching specs/backlog/**) can never fire and the CI backlog-doctor job runs against a folder that never reaches the repo, while removal-on-release writes TRACKED durable copies of consumed entries to specs/_archive — the live set is less durable than its own consumption ledger.
title: specs/backlog/ has no gitignore opt-in: backlog invisible to git while BL-* governance assumes committed backlog
